reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly reports that for AlCoCrFeNi2.1, cryo-rolling and annealing achieved 1.47 GPa strength and 14% elongation, outperforming cold-rolling and annealing (1.2 GPa, 12% elongation). This supports the predicted outcome and the superiority over the baseline. However, E1 provides no microstructural characterization or mechanistic data to support the premises about ultrafine-grained duplex structure formation, increased boundary density, grain-boundary strengthening, or strain partitioning mechanisms.
premises: Cryo-rolling + annealing refines lamellar microstructure into ultrafine-grained duplex structure
Refined structure increases phase and grain boundary density
Grain-boundary strengthening and dislocation hindrance increase strength
Duplex microstructure improves strain partitioning and ductility
Cryo-rolled + annealed EHEA outperforms cold-rolled + annealed baseline in strength and ductility
